questions.evidence: For the most part, the response has been favorable, to say the least. > “Hooray! At last!” wrote Anthony Tommasini, a sober-sided

options.reason: 与原文相反。第一段强调反响正面，没有说任命招致批评。

questions.stem: Tommasini regards Gilbert as an artist who is
questions.evidence: Even Tommasini, who had advocated Gilbert's appointment in the *Times*, calls him “an unpretentious musician with no air of the fo

options.reason: 无中生有。文中没有评价他的影响力，反而说他相对不知名。
`unpretentious` 表示不炫耀、不摆架子，`with no air of the formidable conductor` 进一步说明他没有名指挥家的威严派头，正对应 `modest`。

文中未用该引语判断其才华；作者随后甚至说自己不知道他是否算好指挥家。

questions.stem: According to the text, which of the following is true of recordings?
questions.evidence: These recordings are cheap, available everywhere, and very often much higher in artistic quality than today's live performances; m

options.en: They are often inferior to live concerts in quality.
options.reason: 与原文相反；录音往往 `much higher in artistic quality`。

options.en: They are easily accessible to the general public.
options.reason: `cheap`、`available everywhere` 以及可由听众自主选择时间地点，共同说明录音价格亲民、易于获得，即对一般公众而言很容易接触到。

questions.stem: Regarding Gilbert's role in revitalizing the Philharmonic, the author feels
questions.evidence: For my part, I have no idea whether Gilbert is a great conductor or even a good one. > But what will be the nature of that differe

options.reason: 作者先坦言无法判断吉尔伯特是否优秀，随后质问所谓改变究竟是什么，并指出扩大曲目仍不够、成功还取决于重建观众关系。这一连串保留与条件体现的是怀疑态度。
把他人赞誉误当作者态度。热烈评价来自托马西尼和罗斯，作者本人明显更审慎。
与作者的 `I have no idea` 及条件式表达不符。
